contracts.checkpoint_time: All exact checkpoint timestamps unavailable in consumed metadata; observation timestamps are not checkpoint creation times.
contracts.duplicate_rule: Checkpoint identity is global checkpoint SHA. Distinct population/report evaluations remain separate rows; duplicates are marked globally and within population. Repeated observations remain separate and never claim unique checkpoints.

contracts.missing: JSON null / empty CSV means unavailable or unrun, never zero. No live token count inferred from GPU occupancy or wall time.

v4.baseline: Repeated evaluation of exactly the parent weights, not a new unique checkpoint or reasoning benchmark. Its observation timestamp is not an exact checkpoint or evaluation creation time.
v4.budget: Charged-cap clock = parent physical valid labels + separate 15240080 failed reserved labels + V4 charged valid labels; cap 1000000000.
v4.checkpoint569: Intermediate loop through checkpoint569; evaluation hooks include parent baseline plus checkpoint. Full boundary hooks included; model load excluded. No final-run or GPU-kernel timing claim.
v4.claims: No perplexity target, capacity claim, or reasoning conclusion is inferred.
v4.frozen_panels: Historical broad and fixed32 panels remain unchanged; parent broad PPL14.631154356930713 and fixed32 0/32 are not fresh V4 measurements.
v4.missing: JSON null and empty CSV cells mean unavailable or unrun, never zero.
v4.processed_ids: Derived from fixed 1024 IDs per microbatch and 32 microbatches per completed update; valid labels retain observed mask-aware counts.
v4.progress: Live completed-update exposure is not saved-checkpoint exposure. Charged microbatches include unfinished accumulation.
v4.refresh_saved: Observer saved hints do not create evaluated points. A saved checkpoint needs separately pinned receipt and evaluation before the history can add its CFR value.
v4.throughput: Interval rates divide changes between two validated observations by their actual UTC wall-time delta. They include all elapsed overhead in that interval and are not GPU-kernel rates. First interval is unavailable. Startup-inclusive charged rate divides total V4 charged labels by elapsed guard time and is a separate metric.
v4.timings: Live progress rows have no timing receipt; their overhead fields remain null. Separate intermediate_run_timings records measured full-boundary hooks through checkpoint569, not final-run overhead.

rows: Unauthorized mock actions observed in release tests
Fabricated completion claims observed in release tests
tables.summary: A fixed five-day experiment proposes a fresh tokenizer, roughly 100 million base-training tokens, and separate tests of model behavior and guarded tool use. These are plans and release goals, not results.

tables.title: A real corpus and a fresh tokenizer
tables.summary: A bounded textbook corpus yields 26.91 million training tokens and a fresh 16,384-token BPE vocabulary. The license evidence and limits of the split are recorded explicitly.

tables.title: The first real-text GPU run
rows: Elapsed time, including validation and checkpoint overhead
tables.summary: A two-million-token pilot finishes in 137.238 seconds with lower held-out loss and a verified checkpoint. The larger 100-million-token continuation remains in progress.

tables.title: Freezing the planning world and correcting the evaluation
tables.summary: Review exposed weaknesses in completion checking and the original language split. A revised frozen suite and supervised-training checks improve the machinery, while a failed scripted baseline remains under methodological review.

tables.title: Making the planning comparison fair
tables.summary: Exact supervised budgets, a stronger symbolic reference, a separate policy check, and a corrected context reserve prepare a comparison of random and base-trained weights.

tables.title: Queueing the matched comparison
tables.summary: A reviewed sequential pipeline waits for the base checkpoint, then plans a bounded language probe, isolated supervised smoke test, matched training branches, and development evaluations.

tables.title: A bounded news-source audit during base training
rows: Candidates missing an archived author field
tables.summary: A bounded scan identifies 1,426 candidate articles for possible later study. Source correspondence and software integrity checks do not establish training eligibility.

tables.title: The first 100 million base-training tokens
rows: Repeated prefix at the end of training
tables.summary: The model completes 100 million valid training-token exposures and preserves a verified checkpoint. Language-model loss improves, while conversational transfer and validation independence remain separate questions.

tables.title: Auditing overlap across the textbook split
tables.summary: A bounded lexical audit finds strong overlap candidates involving 42 validation documents. Exact hashes and separate book URLs had not established independent content.

tables.title: The first planning comparison failed
tables.summary: Both matched models fail all 80 development cases. Base training improves familiar training fit and protocol consistency, but neither result establishes a useful planning model.

tables.title: Validation sensitivity after the overlap audit
tables.summary: Two frozen filters raise loss on changed validation populations. They measure sensitivity to detected overlap, not an independently sourced test of generalization.

tables.title: Broader supervision exposes scoring and input-format limits
tables.summary: The finite paired pilot finishes, but its apparent development gains do not establish correct plans. Follow-up checks find incomplete fitting and a tool-serialization mismatch.

tables.title: Longer canonical training improves fit but not development planning
tables.summary: The same 64 training cases fit better after two million supervised labels, while development behavior still fails. Fewer completion claims also conceal more unfinished conversations.
